summary.tldr: Develops a national strategy to decriminalize illegal substances and repeals federal possession offences under the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act.
what_it_does: Requires the Minister of Health to develop a national strategy for decriminalizing illegal substances.
Requires the strategy to be built with consultations on health, justice and public safety, including with First Nations, Inuit and Métis people and organizations.
Says the strategy must consider a possession threshold, a decision maker for that threshold, and an administrative sanctions system that could include warnings, fines or treatment referrals.
Requires a conference within 180 days after the Act comes into force, then a report to Parliament within two years and an online posting within 10 days.
Repeals sections 4 and 4.1 of the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act, ending the federal offence of possessing scheduled substances and removing the related emergency-help exemption.
Updates related definitions and cross-references in the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act, Criminal Code and Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.
who_it_affects: First Nations, Inuit and Métis communities
summary.background: The bill amends the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act, including the parts that now make possession of certain scheduled substances an offence.
